chunks: And Zurārah has narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:
"Whoever does not find the price of the sacrificial animal, and wishes to fast the three days during the last ten days, then there is no harm in that."

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū ʿAbdillāh, Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام
key_terms.الثَّلَاثَةَ الْأَيَّامِ: the three prescribed days of fasting
key_terms.ثَمَنَ الْهَدْيِ: the price of the sacrificial animal required for hajj
key_terms.زُرَارَةُ: Zurārah, the narrator transmitting this hadith
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ: there is no harm in that; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Can a pilgrim who cannot afford the sacrificial animal fast the three days during the last ten days of Dhul-Hijjah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the mutamatti' who cannot afford the sacrificial animal required in hajj. It permits fasting the three days in the last ten days, indicating flexibility in fulfilling this obligation when one lacks the financial means.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3100 - Zurara narrated from Abu Abdullah (as) that he said: "
If someone cannot afford the price of a sacrificial animal and wishes to fast the three days during the last ten days (of Dhul-Hijjah), there is no harm in that."
